provenance.title: VBA God Module
provenance.metric: patterns[name === "VBA God Module"].files — analyzed files where isCode !== false && functions.length > 20 (index.html:1414 detectPatterns `vbaGodFiles`). `VBA God Module` is `God Object` (> 15) at a higher ceiling over the same parser count, so every sibling is landed <= 15 where the reduction is in-gate. `functions` comes from the headless parser: for `.js/.jsx/.ts/.tsx/.mjs/.cjs/.vue/.svelte` the served UI parses with acorn (after Babel strips TS/JSX), so object-literal methods and arrow properties count; the codeflow `run-analysis.mjs` sandbox leaves acorn/Babel undefined and falls back to `heuristic-regex`, which does NOT count them. The browser export that filed this issue used the acorn-babel mode (totalFunctions 4975 on the filed snapshot); the regex mode reports a different, smaller set (19 on the base).
provenance.filesNote: `files` is the analyzer's own `summary.totalFiles` for the snapshot. Only its ordering matters here: `after.files > before.files` proves the drop did not come from deleting files. `.mts`/`.json`/`.md` are not in `codeExts`, so the oracle and this fixture add no parsed file.
provenance.filedNote: the issue was filed with 25 files at analyzedAt 1791804971015 against the then-main. That snapshot predates #2006 (the two Python test modules still counted 21 each) and #2057. The re-measured immutable base below (origin/main c89a4d27) also reports 25, but with those two Python modules already split and two files the issue did not cite (disk_space_test.go, fp-filter.js) newly over the ceiling.
provenance.afterNote: `after` is the delivered working tree measured before the pipeline's commit: the four `.pi/extensions` splits add ten `.ts` siblings (`.ts` is scored, every sibling lands <= 15) and no scored function is added, renamed or removed beyond the moved declarations.

tradeoffs.vbaGodModule: 25 -> 21 flagged files (-4). The four reduced `.pi/extensions` modules carried object-literal stubs, JSON-kind extractors and dialog helpers the acorn-babel parser counts as declarations; whole cohesive blocks moved verbatim into siblings, and each reduced module re-exports its public surface so no importer changed.
tradeoffs.godObject: 36 -> 32 flagged files: the expected co-benefit (VBA God Module is a strict subset of God Object). Every sibling lands <= 15, so no sibling mints a God Object regression.
tradeoffs.functions: 4244 -> 4241 parsed declarations. No test was added, removed or renamed: the four suites still run the same tests, and every public export keeps its name.
tradeoffs.approach: verbatim moves plus re-export barrels: `harness-fixtures.ts` spreads two new stub factories, `normalize.ts` merges two kind tables and re-exports the moved types, `debug.ts` re-exports the logger factory, `config-ui.test.ts` hands its dialog suite to a sibling with a shared theme mock. `npm test` and `npm run tsc:extensions` are the verification burden.
tradeoffs.notDone: the 16 `.rs` files (no toolchain), the embedded `run-analysis.mjs` and `server.py` (Dockerfile COPY / served-contract boundaries) and `mock-pi.ts` (needs ~8 modules) stay flagged and are recorded as deferred with a reason each.

deferred.reason: mock-pi.ts (93 declarations under the acorn-babel parser) is one ExtensionScore mock whose whole surface is object-literal stubs; bringing every sibling <= 15 needs roughly eight section modules and is deferred to its own recorded change (architecture trade-off), matching #2004's deferral of the 106-declaration test suite.

the embedded headless analyzer: a split adds an `.mjs` sibling that the codeflow Dockerfile COPY set, the `//go:embed embedded` set and the Go asset/run tests must own in the same change, so it is deferred to the change that owns that boundary (#2004 precedent).

`server.py` (51 declarations) is the codeflow bridge: moving code out of it changes the Dockerfile COPY set and the `_BRIDGE_JS`/`_UI_REWRITES` served contract pinned by the shim smoke/bridge tests, so it is deferred to the change that owns that boundary guard (#2006 reason).

no Rust toolchain in the pipeline image — `which cargo/rustc` is empty, there is no Docker in-gate and no workflow compiles `embedded/docker/ui` (its builder image needs `rust:1.99`), so a split under that tree could not be compiled or tested before landing (#2002–#2006 precedent).

flagged on the delivered tree but NOT cited by #2036 (the issue's list predates #2057, which reshaped these files); owned by the long-file / anti-pattern issues that share the same file set, not by this reduction.
